title: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (April 2027) — the edition that settled the month-shape question, and settled it against both forks
source: EST: eia.gov/outlooks/steo/release_schedule.php, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 54,906 bytes — a FIFTH byte-identical pull, after the eia-steo-2026-12-08 lane's 2026-09-08 fetch and the 2027-01-12, 2027-02-09 and 2027-03-09 lanes' 2026-09-09 fetches). Read from the RAW HTML table rather than a converted rendering (sibling lanes recorded a markdown converter shifting this page's Notes column by one row): the 2027 row is "April 2027 | 04/06/2027" with a blank Notes cell, and the same page states the release window as 12:00 pm-12:15 pm ET. Reproduces independently from the page's own rule — "the first Tuesday following the first Thursday of each month", with the footnote "If a Federal holiday falls on the Monday before the normal release date the release is delayed until Wednesday": 2027-04-01 is a Thursday, the following Tuesday is 04-06, and 2027-04-05 is a Monday carrying no Federal holiday (the 2027 Federal calendar has none in April). STRONGER THAN THE SIBLING'S DERIVATION ON ONE POINT: both of the footnote's 2027 firings sit in the same table and both reproduce from the rule — "July 2027 | 07/07/2027 (Wednesday)" because July 4, 2027 is a Sunday observed Monday July 5, and "September 2027 | 09/08/2027 (Wednesday)" because Labor Day 2027 is Monday September 6 — so the exception is demonstrably live inside the very year being dated, and it does not apply here. Filed estimate on the two standing counts every EIA entry here records, neither of them date doubt: this calendar defines no `confirmed` prefix for the EIA, and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: Canonical entry written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), promoting the sole prior proposal eia-steo-2027-04-06.from-eia-steo-2027-03-09.json. That proposal named 04-06 as the DISCRIMINATOR between two readings of the sibling chain's month-shape finding: either MARCH SPECIFICALLY is elevated (and April reverts to the ordinary mean) or EVERYTHING AFTER FEBRUARY is elevated (and the whole stickiness frame is a February artifact). BOTH FORKS FAIL, and the fork itself was false. This session extended the measurement from two out-year series to FOUR (2023, 2024, 2025, 2026) and switched the primary from the report PDFs to EIA's own machine-readable archive files, eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/<edition>_base.xlsx, which carry the unrounded series and reproduce every rounded Table 7a total in the sibling's table exactly. (1) THE MONTH-SHAPE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED OUT OF SAMPLE. On the total US electricity-consumption line (series ELCOTWH, annual sum of the newly-rolled out-year), March ranks 9th of 11 revisions in the 2023 series and 10th of 11 in the 2024 series, against 2nd in 2025 and 2nd of 7 in 2026. Mean absolute move: February 0.178%, March 0.363%, April 0.271%, every month from May onward 0.330% (n=28). Drop 2025 and the picture inverts — February 0.134%, March 0.181%, April 0.097% against 0.321% for May onward — so the early-year editions move that line LESS than the later ones, which is the opposite of the second fork. Per-year mean |delta| is 0.235% (2023), 0.334% (2024), 0.440% (2025), 0.198% (2026): THE VARIANCE LIVES IN THE YEAR, NOT THE MONTH, and 2025 is the outlier year the sibling's n=2 window happened to contain. (2) BUT THE STICKINESS FINDING ITSELF SURVIVES, ON A NON-EDITORIAL BASKET, WITH A REAL P-VALUE FOR THE FIRST TIME. The sibling measured the out-year/near-year revision ratio off each edition's own `Notable forecast changes` table and flagged the limit itself — EIA chooses which 3 to 8 lines are notable. Recomputed on a FIXED 9-series basket present in all 44 archived editions (WTIPUUS, BREPUUS, NGHHUUS, NGRCUUS, ESRCUUS, ELCOTWH, NGTCPUS, NGPRPUS, COPRPUS) over 40 within-series edition pairs, the four February editions score 0.617, 0.457, 0.386 and 0.321 — ranks 8, 5, 3 and 1 of 40 — against a 1.62 mean for May onward. Exact one-sided Mann-Whitney: February vs every other edition p=0.00042; February vs April p=0.0143 with ZERO OVERLAP across four years; February vs March p=0.029; March vs April p=0.10, i.e. NOT separable. (3) THE RIGHT SHAPE IS A DECAY, NOT A STEP OR A SPIKE: mean ratio 0.445 (Feb) -> 0.794 (Mar) -> 1.136 (Apr) -> 1.618 (May onward). By April the out-year is revised about as hard as the near year, which is what this edition is actually for. (4) THE APRIL TAPE COHORT IS A SECOND CONFOUND, AND THE RULE IS NOW PROVEN TWICE WITH INDEPENDENT CAUSES. Median full-day |move| on the two in-window April editions reads NVDA 3.09%, SPY 2.21%, ^VIX 13.89%, MRVL 6.69%, AVGO 6.58%, CRWV 9.39% — which decomposes into 2025-04-10 (SPY -4.38%, NVDA -5.91%, ^VIX +21.12%), the session AFTER the tariff-pause reversal, inside a 2025-04-01..04-21 window whose own SPY max is +10.50% on 04-09 and whose NVDA max is +18.72% the same day; and 2026-04-07 (SPY +0.04%, CL=F +0.48%, NVDA +0.26%), a dead-quiet session inside a window where CL=F fell 16.41% the very NEXT day. may26.pdf names its own cause: Brent "reaching a high of $138 per barrel (b) on April 7" — the STEO release day was the apex of a war spike and moved nothing close to close. The March lane withdrew its crude cohort as one war averaged with one ordinary day; the April cohort is one tariff crash averaged with one dead session. Two for two, and the pooled null (n=24) reproduced to the cent on a FIFTH independent pipeline. (5) CORRIDOR — the cleanest of the chain: within +/-4 days this calendar tracks NOTHING; at -5 it tracks japan-food-tax-cut-2027-04-01 and the proposal-only uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01, both policy effective-dates rather than prints. The eight sessions AFTER 04-06 are empty until tic-monthly-2027-04-15 (+9, proposal-only) and opex-2027-04-16 (+10). Per the Fed primary (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09, "Last Update: August 19, 2026") the April 2027 meeting is Apr 27-28 with NO Summary of Economic Projections, so its blackout opens 2027-04-17 and this edition publishes 11 days before it — a FOURTH distinct Fed position after 01-12 (four days before a blackout), 02-09 (none) and 03-09 (inside one, day 4, seven days before a SEP), and the only one with no Fed proximity at all. (6) THE AEO NOTE THE MARCH LANE LEFT FOR THIS LANE IS CORRECTED DOWNWARD. EIA's own pressroom (eia.gov/pressroom/releases.php, fetched 2026-09-09) dates "EIA releases the Annual Energy Outlook 2026" to April 8, 2026 — ONE DAY AFTER the April 2026 STEO — which is a real adjacency. But eia.gov/outlooks/aeo/archive.php (HTTP 200, 82,111 bytes, same day) lists archived editions beginning at 2023 while the live product is AEO2026: NO AEO2024 AND NO AEO2025 EXIST. The AEO has just come off a two-year gap and eia.gov/outlooks/aeo/ still commits only to a bare "Next Release Date: 2027", so an AEO2027 landing beside this edition is a one-observation pattern on a product that skipped two of the last three years. Recorded, undatable, not proposed. (7) NOTHING IS PROPOSED FROM THIS SWEEP, DELIBERATELY. The chain's question is answered and the null has now survived a fifth pipeline and two decomposed confounds; proposing the May 2027 edition would be the calendar completeness this chain refuses. Filed `low` on the sibling entries' reasoning and the pooled tape.
